landing.title: Your project and your AI in one place, from analysis to code to launch
landing.subtitle: The AI you already use, plugged into your project's corpus. Your workspaces run on your machines or on ours, and everything is followed from a single page.
landing.step1Body: You describe your project to your AI, in the client you already use. The backlog and the documentation get written as you talk — and they stay.
landing.step2Body: Development starts from that same conversation. Workspace, test environment, quality measured: nothing to set up by hand.
landing.step3Body: Site, announcement and documentation are written from the project's corpus — the very one used to build it.
landing.why1Body: The project's corpus is the memory; a conversation is only a window onto it. Picking it up three weeks later costs no context to rebuild.
landing.why2Title: The agent sees what it does
landing.why2Body: Project context, quality measured continuously, logs and metrics centralised by default. It never has to beg for a trace after a failure.
landing.why3Body: Six agents supported — Claude, Cline, Copilot, Cursor, Windsurf, Kimi Code — and two modes at parity: as a service, or on your own machines. The FSL licence is what makes both possible.

guide.title: How to create the client in Keycloak
guide.intro: In your realm (the one in the Issuer URL above):
guide.step1: Clients → Create client → type OpenID Connect, Client ID: workspace-portal.
guide.step2: Enable “Client authentication” (confidential client) and keep only “Standard flow”.
guide.step3: Set the Valid redirect URI to exactly this value:
guide.step5: Open the Credentials tab, copy the Client secret, and paste it in the field above.
guide.step6: Realm roles → create “dev” and “admin”, then assign them to users (Users → Role mapping).
guide.step7: Client scopes → roles → mapper “realm roles” → enable “Add to ID token”. Otherwise roles stay empty and access is denied (the portal reads roles from the ID token).

network.title: Network configuration
network.intro: Public domain and URL of the portal. Setting the base domain enables workspace exposure by sub-domain (https://ws-xxx.<domain>).

network.externalUrlHint: Absolute public URL of the portal, e.g. https://dev.yoops.org.
network.resolveEmpty: Enter a hostname or IP first.
network.workspaceHostHint: Optional. LAN IP of the machine hosting the portal container, used to build direct workspace URLs when there is no sub-domain routing (dev mode). All workspace tunnels terminate on the portal, so a single value covers every node. E.g. 192.168.10.50.
network.cookieDomainHint: Root domain for the session cookie, e.g. yoops.org. Required when the portal (dev.yoops.org) and the VS Code proxy (vs-dev.yoops.org) share a common ancestor. Takes effect immediately — no restart needed.

logs.enabledHint: When off, the portal injects no collector, hides the Logs link, and disables the logs_query MCP tool.
logs.lokiPushUrlHint: Must be reachable from every host, including remote test servers — an IP/hostname, not a Docker service name. E.g. http://192.168.10.196:3100/loki/api/v1/push.
logs.lokiQueryUrlHint: Used by the logs_query MCP tool, running inside the portal — the internal Docker service name works, e.g. http://loki:3100.
logs.grafanaUrlHint: Public URL used for the Logs link and Grafana deep-links, e.g. https://log.dev.yoops.org.
logs.moduleHint: Common 'module' label applied to every collector (default: devpod).
logs.pushTokenHint: Optional — only if Loki requires auth. Literal value or ${vault://...}/${env://...} reference. Leave empty to keep the current one.
logs.missingUrls: Loki push URL and query URL are required to enable centralized logs.
logs.metricsPushUrlHint: remote_write endpoint of the TSDB. Injected into metrics collectors as METRICS_URL, the way LOKI_URL is injected into log collectors — changing it realigns already-deployed collectors. Empty: no metrics collector will start.

billing.title: Billing catalog
billing.description: Where we sell, in which currency, and through which payment channel. Getting this wrong means charging a customer at the wrong rate.
billing.countriesEmpty: No country yet. Without an enabled country, no offer can be proposed.
billing.countryHelp: The ISO code is the country's identity: it cannot be renamed. Currencies and channels are saved along with the form.
billing.currenciesHelp: What the platform can charge in — independent of the buyer's country. Exactly one default currency: the one proposed when nothing else applies.
billing.attachedProvidersHelp: Checked in trial order: one failing channel must not lose the sale.
billing.providersEmpty: No payment channel. Create one before attaching it to a country.
billing.providerHelp: No API key is typed here: you point at an existing secret. The tax mode decides whether the platform sends net or gross amounts.
billing.slugHelp: Identifies the instance, not the adapter: two Stripe accounts can coexist.

taxModeHelp.manuel: The platform computes tax from the rate table and sends gross amounts.
taxModeHelp.automatique: The provider computes tax: the platform sends net amounts.

billing.secretHelp: Reference into the secrets table. The value is never read nor displayed here.
billing.stripeAccountHelp: Account identifier (acct_…). Leave empty until the account is opened.
billing.stripeWebhookSecretHelp: Reference to the secret holding the whsec_… of the endpoint declared on the Stripe side. Without it, webhook signatures cannot be verified.
billing.webhookUrlHelp: Declare it as-is in the provider's dashboard (Stripe: with the pinned API version). The provider will call this address.
billing.configHelp: Fields specific to the adapter kind (Stripe: account_id, webhook_secret_slug…). An unknown key is rejected on save.
billing.taxRatesHelp: A rate is never edited: it is closed, and a new one takes over. That is what keeps an old invoice reproducible with the rate of its time.
billing.taxRatesEmpty: No rate yet. In manual mode, the platform cannot compute tax.
billing.taxRatesAfterSave: Tax rates can be added once the country is saved.
billing.currenciesEmpty: No currency yet. Without an enabled currency, no offer can be published.

offers.title: Subscription offers
offers.description: What we sell, at what price and in which currency. A published offer with no price in an enabled currency could not be proposed to anyone.
offers.empty: No offer yet. Nothing is sellable until an offer is published.
offers.help: The amount you type is net or gross depending on the tax mode of the selected channel — the screen states it next to the prices.
offers.priorityHelp: Position on the public plans page, ascending: 0 shows first. Ties are broken by slug.
offers.tacitRenewalOn: At term, the plan starts over for the same duration and the customer is charged again. The law requires informing them before the deadline.
offers.tacitRenewalOff: At term, the plan stops. The customer must take it again to continue.
offers.oncePerAccountOn: An account that already subscribed to this offer cannot take it again. This is what bounds a welcome offer.
offers.oncePerAccountOff: The offer can be subscribed to as many times as wanted by the same account.
offers.quotaHelp: Empty field = unlimited. Both quotas are independent, and the machine's physical capacity always takes precedence.

priceMeaning.manuel: Channel in manual mode: the amount is gross, the platform has already computed tax.
priceMeaning.automatique: Channel in automatic mode: the amount is net, the provider will add tax.

offers.missingCurrencies: Enabled currencies without a price: {{list}}. The offer will not be proposed there.
offers.providerPriceIdHint: Price id at the provider (Stripe: “price_…”). Optional — leave empty until a price exists there. If set, the provider's price is what gets charged, so both amounts must stay in agreement.
offers.shortNameHelp: The product name — “Standard”, “Max”. It is not translated: this is what appears in administration and logs. The slug derives from it.
offers.heading: Title shown to the customer
offers.pricesIncludeTaxOn: Tax included: the amount is what the customer will pay.
offers.pricesIncludeTaxOff: Tax excluded: tax will be added to the amount entered.
offers.autoCurrenciesHelp: Accepted currencies without their own price are derived from the default price, markup included. This is not an exchange rate: it is a commercial markup, and it follows no market.
offers.noAcceptedCurrency: No accepted currency. Declare some in the billing catalog before pricing this offer.
offers.champsManquantsGeneral: The short name or the slug is missing.
offers.durationHelp: Every plan is time-boxed: a trial because it must end, a paid plan because a subscription without a term cannot be billed. The expiry carries a day AND a time. Required to publish.
offers.durationExample: A subscriber signing up now would see their plan expire in {{jours}} days, on {{echeance}} — the time of day is kept, to the minute.
offers.isFreeOn: No price: the offer exists to try the product, and stops at the end of its duration.
offers.isFreeOff: Paid offer: at least one price in an accepted currency is required to publish it.
offers.freeNoPricing: Free offer: there is nothing to price. Its duration is set in the “Duration” tab.
offers.champsManquantsDuree: A published offer must have a duration.
offers.variablesHelp: Free key/value parameters of the offer (VM template, host capacity…), injected into the debut_essai and activation events at subscription time.
offers.noVariable: No variable — the offer injects no parameter into provisioning.
offers.variableExists: This key is already set — remove it first to replace it.
offers.hostProfilesHelp: The host profiles this offer can open, from highest to lowest priority. A host profile carries the machine profile, hence the hypervisor type and the creation script: without one, nothing would say which machine to open on subscription. Order is priority — the first one is tried first.
offers.noHostProfile: No host profile. The offer can still be saved, but publishing requires at least one.
offers.noHostProfileLeft: Every host profile is already listed
offers.champsManquantsProfils: A host profile is missing: nothing would say which machine to open.

patHelp.title: How do I get a Personal Access Token (PAT)?
patHelp.intro: A PAT lets the portal clone and push your private Git repositories on your behalf. Create one on your provider, then register it here. Use the minimum scopes and set an expiration date.
patHelp.github: GitHub — Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens (or Tokens (classic)) → Generate token. Grant Contents: Read and write (fine-grained) or the repo scope (classic). Copy the token (github_pat_… or ghp_…).
patHelp.gitlab: GitLab — Preferences → Access Tokens → Add new token. Select the read_repository and write_repository scopes (or api). Copy the token (glpat-…).
patHelp.bitbucket: Bitbucket Cloud — Personal settings → App passwords → Create app password. Grant Repositories: Read and Write; use it as the token. (Bitbucket Data Center: Manage account → HTTP access tokens.)
patHelp.azure: Azure DevOps — User settings → Personal access tokens → New Token. Grant the Code (Read & Write) scope. Copy the token.

consent.title: Authorize access
consent.intro: An application requests access to your MCP gateway. Select a profile to define which services it may use.
consent.noProfiles: No profile yet. Create one in the MCP settings first.

mcp.title: MCP Gateway
mcp.info: Federate several MCP servers behind a single gateway and control which services each client may use.
mcp.webHint: Add this URL as a custom connector in Claude. Sign-in uses OAuth — you pick the services on the consent screen. Nothing to create here.
mcp.desktopHint: Issue an apikey below and paste it into the client config (Authorization: Bearer).

profiles.name: Name
profiles.empty: No profile yet. Create one to start exposing services.
profiles.noToolsCatalog: No tools indexed yet (backend not synced).
profiles.unexposeWarning: Unchecking immediately revokes the workspace MCP keys derived from this profile and regenerates the agent configuration files on the fly.
profiles.unexposeDone: Profile removed from workspaces — {{count}} workspace(s) affected.
profiles.exposeSwapWarning: Only one profile can be exposed at a time: “{{previous}}” will be unchecked and its MCP keys revoked. Agents currently working will be disconnected and must restart their session (or run /mcp) to resume.
profiles.exposeSwapped: “{{name}}” is no longer exposed — agents need to reconnect.

step1.title: Copy the gateway URL
step1.desc: Copy the MCP gateway URL displayed above — you'll need it to configure the connector.

step2.title: Open Claude.ai → Settings → Integrations
step2.desc: Go to claude.ai, open the Settings panel, then click "Integrations" (or "Custom connectors" depending on your plan).

step3.title: Add a custom connector
step3.desc: Click "Add integration" and paste the gateway URL. Claude will auto-discover the OAuth metadata.

step4.title: Authenticate via Keycloak
step4.desc: A consent screen opens. Sign in with your Keycloak account (same as the portal), then choose the MCP profile to expose.

step5.title: Start using tools in Claude
step5.desc: The integration is now active. Ask Claude to use a tool — it will call the gateway transparently.

claude.note: OAuth tokens are short-lived and refresh automatically. You do not need to issue an API key for this mode.

step1.title: Copy the gateway URL
step1.desc: Copy the MCP gateway URL displayed above.

step2.title: Open ChatGPT → Settings → Connected apps (or GPT editor → Actions)
step2.desc: In ChatGPT Plus/Team settings, go to "Connected apps". For a custom GPT, open the editor and click "Add actions".

step3.title: Paste the gateway URL and import the schema
step3.desc: The gateway exposes an OpenAPI schema at /openapi.json. ChatGPT will auto-import it. Set the authentication type to OAuth 2.0.

step4.title: Authenticate and select a profile
step4.desc: A Keycloak consent screen opens. Sign in and choose the MCP profile to grant to this ChatGPT session.

openai.note: OAuth tokens are short-lived. If your session expires, reconnect from the ChatGPT settings panel.

gemini.procedureTitle: Connecting Gemini / Google AI Studio via OAuth

step1.title: Copy the gateway URL
step1.desc: Copy the MCP gateway URL displayed above.

step2.title: Open Google AI Studio → Extensions → Add a tool
step2.desc: In AI Studio (aistudio.google.com), open the Extensions panel and click "Add custom tool" or "Connect via MCP".

step3.title: Paste the gateway URL
step3.desc: Enter the MCP gateway URL. Gemini will auto-discover the tool list. Select OAuth 2.0 as the auth method.

step4.title: Authenticate and select a profile
step4.desc: A Keycloak consent screen opens. Sign in and choose the MCP profile to expose to Gemini.

gemini.note: If Google AI Studio does not yet support OAuth MCP natively, use a Client API key (Bearer) from the "Client API Keys" tab as a fallback.

mistral.procedureTitle: Connecting Le Chat / Mistral via OAuth

step1.title: Copy the gateway URL
step1.desc: Copy the MCP gateway URL displayed above.

step2.title: Open Le Chat → Settings → Integrations → MCP
step2.desc: In Le Chat (chat.mistral.ai), open Settings, then the Integrations section and click "Add an MCP server".

step3.title: Paste the gateway URL
step3.desc: Enter the MCP gateway URL. Le Chat supports Streamable HTTP transport. Set auth to OAuth 2.0.

step4.title: Authenticate and select a profile
step4.desc: A Keycloak consent screen opens. Sign in and choose the MCP profile to expose to Mistral.

mistral.note: Le Chat MCP integration is available on Pro plans. Use a Client API key as a fallback for API / agent usage.

explore.title: MCP Explore
explore.subtitle: Explore an MCP server that exposes services before registering it.
explore.searchNeedsSource: Configure a source above to search.
explore.noSources: No source configured — add one to search a catalog.

backends.name: Name
backends.authSchemeHint: How the key is sent to the server. "Bearer" (Authorization: Bearer) by default; "X-API-Key" for servers that require it.
backends.forwardIdentityHint: Adds a signed identity of the logged-in user to calls (x-portal-actor* headers). Enable only for a trusted service that verifies it (docflow, rag, workflow). Requires a key.
backends.appUrlHint: Optional web link shown in the list to open the application.
backends.namespaceImmutable: The namespace cannot be changed after creation.
backends.quarantineHint: Redefinition detected (rug-pull protection). The primitive is hidden and denied until approved.
backends.quarantineApproved: {{name}} approved — the primitive is exposed again
backends.quarantineDisabledLabel: Do not apply the quarantine protection to primitives
backends.quarantineDisabledHint: Trusted backend: tool redefinitions are accepted without approval. Existing quarantines are lifted on save.

apikeys.label: Label
apikeys.tokenOnceWarning: Copy this value now — it will not be shown again.
apikeys.workspaceHint: Key generated by the portal for this workspace — profile managed automatically, revoke only.
apikeys.rotateNeedsRunning: Start the workspace to rotate its key (the new token is re-injected into it).
apikeys.rotatedWarning: The old key is revoked. Copy the new one now — it will not be shown again.
apikeys.rotatedReinjected: Key rotated and re-injected into workspace {{ws}} — the previous generation expires after the grace window.
apikeys.pinnedHint: Profile pinned on this workspace — kept even after a key rotation. Pick “Default” to follow the exposed profile again.

message.title: Service message
message.description: Contextual message for this deployed service
message.none: No message available for this deployment

form.name: Name
form.messageKeyHint: Key of the Jinja2 template to render as a workspace message when the service starts (e.g. service-docker-compose). Leave empty for no message.

autoStart.label: Auto-start on my test machines
autoStart.dialogHint: This template requires values before it can be deployed automatically on every new test machine you create.

catalog.filter: Filter by name, tag or image…
catalog.hint: Click Refresh to load the catalog.

gallery.title: Template gallery
gallery.overwriteConfirmDescription: Template {{key}} / {{culture}} already exists. Importing will overwrite its current content.

profile.title: My profile
profile.identityHint: GUID forwarded to services (workflow, rag, doc) when a backend has "Forward my identity" enabled, to attribute objects created by your agents to you. Generate one (or enter one) and set the SAME value on the service side. Left empty: no identity forwarded.

token.title: Identity token (OIDC)
token.intro: Essential properties of the token received at login. The raw token is never exposed.
token.empty: No claims available (sign in via OIDC).
token.subHint: Copy the "sub" and paste it into the Identity field above (OBO matching), or into the other apps (docflow, rag, workflow).

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.intro: Time zone used to display dates and times across the interface.
timezone.label: Time zone

termix.title: My Termix servers
termix.hint: Termix is the web interface giving you SSH/terminal access to your workspaces. Here are the Termix server(s) linked to your account (up to 3, for redundancy and migrations). The association is managed by an administrator.
termix.none: No Termix server linked (the default server will be used).

culture.title: Language
culture.intro: Your account language. It is stored on the server and also selects the language of the messages sent to you — unlike the quick switch in the bar, which only applies to this browser.
culture.label: Account language

billingAddress.title: Billing address
billingAddress.intro: Used for your payments and invoices. Encrypted on the portal side.
billingAddress.figee: Changing this address does not affect past subscriptions: the address on an issued invoice is frozen, like its price.

agentMessages.title: Inter-agent requests
agentMessages.description: Pending messages between your agent workspaces. You decide to deliver them to a session or reject them.

deliver.title: Deliver to {{ws}}
deliver.description: Pick the target session. A message is never injected into a session that is currently working.
deliver.noSession: No active session — open a session to deliver.

applications.title: Applications
applications.intro: Your important applications, one click away.
applications.iconHint: An emoji, or an https image URL. Auto-detected from the URL when possible.
applications.urlHint: URL must start with http:// or https://
applications.empty: No application yet. Click “Add” to create your first shortcut.
applications.emptyUser: No application has been published by an administrator yet.

skills.title: Skills (skills.sh)
skills.subtitle: Search skills for your agents. “Add” creates a validation request — no skill is ever usable without explicit human validation.
skills.noGrants: No request or granted skill yet.

actionDone.revoke: Grant revoked — routing cut on all placements.

ws.title: Skills of workspace {{name}}
ws.empty: No skill installed in this workspace.
ws.installedUnverified: Installed but NOT verified (content drifted) — re-validation required, no routing.
ws.removed: Skill removed from workspace (grant remains valid).
ws.hint: Installation pulls the current version (npx skills add, no key). If content drifted from the approved hash, the skill is marked unverified and not routed.

automations.title: Automations
automations.intro: On a journal event, call an OpenAPI contract operation. Priority-ordered evaluation, persistent cursor, replay protection.

form.label: Label
form.delayHint: 0 = immediate. Sliding window: waits for the event to settle.
form.missing: Label, events, contract, operation and URL are required.
form.slugHint: Stable identifier, derived from the label. Editable.
form.filterIntro: Preliminary API call (e.g. “does the user exist?”). Test the call, then set an evaluation rule that gates the Call tab.
form.headersShared: Headers shared with the Call tab (the apikey serves both filter and call).
form.secretSystemHint: System (admin) secret, resolved by the automation in the background — distinct from your profile secrets (PIN-encrypted, unreadable in the background). Enter the raw value (e.g. “tmx_…”, without “Bearer”).
form.evalHint: Rule applied to the response: JSONPath (with {variable}) then operator. If the rule fails, the Call tab request is not executed.

contracts.title: OpenAPI contracts
contracts.intro: Imported (reusable) contracts describing operations callable by automations.
contracts.label: Label
contracts.pasteHint: If pasted, the URL is ignored (manual import, no refresh).
contracts.needUrlOrSpec: Provide a URL or a spec
contracts.editUrlHint: Changing the URL re-fetches the spec. Clearing the URL freezes the contract (manual import).

events.title: Event journal
events.intro: All events stored in the journal (app_event), newest first. #seq is the automations' cursor id.
events.replayHint: Move the global cursor just before this event to re-evaluate everything.
events.replayConfirm: Re-evaluate all rules from event #{{seq}}? The global cursor rewinds and the affected runs are cleared.
events.replayed: Cursor repositioned ({{automations}} automation(s)) — re-evaluation on next sweep.

tree.title: Rule tree
tree.intro: Blocks run in sequence: filter (gate) → calls → child blocks. A failed filter skips the subtree and continues with the next sibling.
tree.empty: No blocks — the rule does nothing.
tree.noFilter: No filter — the block always passes.

editor.missing: Label and trigger events are required.
editor.headersShared: Headers shared by ALL calls and filters of the rule.
editor.sampleVarsHint: Used by the “Test call” buttons to render {variable}; at run time the event values are used.
editor.eventVars: Variables exposed by these events (click to copy):
